generic.title: Important disclaimer
paragraphs: This calculator provides an indicative estimate of your pay entitlement for the hours entered. It should not be used to make, process, approve or determine employee payments. It is not legal, industrial relations, payroll, taxation or accounting advice and should not be relied upon to determine an employee’s legal entitlement or an employer’s payroll obligation.

Results depend on the information entered and the rules configured in the calculator. Any payment decision must be made using the applicable industrial instrument, employment contract, roster and payroll records, with appropriate payroll, legal or industrial-relations review where required.
For accurate workplace pay and entitlement information, please contact the Fair Work Ombudsman or visit fairwork.gov.au.

Testing access only: named accounts use a shared password and are intended only for controlled testing. Full user authentication is not yet live. Do not use these accounts for sensitive or production data.

fast_food.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This model is a guide to selected adult employee payments under the Fast Food Industry Award 2020. It applies the configured ordinary-hour limits, casual loading, minimum paid engagements for part-time and casual employees, weekday late-night and early-morning penalties, weekend and public-holiday rates, daily and period overtime thresholds, and two-tier Monday-to-Saturday overtime rates.
assumptions: The selected instrument, classification, employment type, base hourly rate and entered shift details are correct, and the employee is covered by the Fast Food Industry Award 2020 without an enterprise agreement or other overriding arrangement.
The two entered weeks form one chronological fortnight. Full-time ordinary hours are assessed against 76 hours for that fortnight; part-time and casual period thresholds are assessed weekly.

For a part-time employee, the contracted-hours entry is the employee’s current agreed ordinary hours per week. The calculator uses that entry as the weekly overtime threshold, or 38 hours per week if no contracted-hours value is supplied.
Entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks, public-holiday selections and any manual ordinary-time or overtime selections accurately reflect the employee’s records and applicable arrangements.
A manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the entire entered shift, and the user has determined that classification is appropriate.
limitations: The Award’s five-days-per-week rule, including the exception permitting 6 days in one week where no more than 4 days are worked in the following week, is approximated by a maximum of 10 worked days across the entered fortnight.

Roster-based overtime is supported through manual classification. The user identifies hours worked outside a full-time employee’s roster or the days, start and finish times, and meal breaks in a part-time employee’s agreed or validly varied regular pattern.
Sunday ordinary-hour penalties default to the Level 1 rate. The higher Sunday ordinary-hour rates for Level 2 and Level 3 employees are not selected automatically.

Entered unpaid breaks are deducted from worked time, and a 30-minute unpaid break is used where no break duration is supplied. Break entitlement and compliance remain matters for review against the roster and Award.

Public holidays and manual classifications are user-selected. The user confirms the applicable date, location and substitution arrangements and, where only part of a shift requires manual classification, enters that part as a separate shift segment.
exclusions: The configured scope is limited to the rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above. Rules outside that scope include the examples below.
The 4-hour minimum payment for Sunday overtime that is not continuous with ordinary hours.
Junior, apprentice, trainee, supported-wage and school-based trainee rates.
Classification progression, higher duties, future annual wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Allowances and reimbursements, including meals, uniforms, cold work, travel, vehicle use and other expenses.
Split or broken shifts, recalls, call-backs, time off instead of overtime, and minimum-payment rules other than the configured part-time and casual minimum engagements.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Enterprise agreements, annualised salaries, individual flexibility arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that may apply instead of, or alongside, the Award.
closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

woolies_2024_demo.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This calculator estimates pay for the hours entered using selected rules from the Woolworths Australian Food Group Agreement 2024. It calculates ordinary pay, casual loading, minimum paid engagements, weekday and weekend penalties, public-holiday rates, overtime, shiftwork rates and insufficient-break payments.
assumptions: The employee is a wages-paid team member covered by the Woolworths Australian Food Group Agreement 2024, and the selected classification, employment type and worker type are correct.

Select or enter the adult non-casual base hourly rate for the employee’s classification. For casual employees, the calculator applies both the casual loading and any applicable penalty or overtime rate.
The two entered weeks are assumed to be one pay period.

The calculator applies an insufficient-break payment when the employee has fewer than 10 hours between shifts. This assumes the employee has agreed to reduce the standard gap between shifts to 10 hours (clause 7.3).

Part-time employees are assumed to have agreed to work above their contracted hours as flex-up hours. These hours are treated as ordinary hours until the employee exceeds 38 hours in a week (clause 8.4).
Shiftworkers are assumed to be employees who were hired as shiftworkers and are rostered solely for shiftwork during the week. All entered shifts are treated as shiftwork shifts.
The entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks and public-holiday selections accurately reflect the employee’s roster and payroll records.
Any manual ordinary-time or overtime selection is assumed to be correct and applies to the whole entered shift.
limitations: The calculator covers the two entered weeks. It applies a 76-hour full-time threshold and a maximum of 10 worked days across the fortnight. Four-week roster requirements should be reviewed separately against the employee’s roster.
The first entered shift above 9 ordinary hours in a week is treated as the permitted shift of up to 11 ordinary hours. The user should confirm that this is the employee’s rostered long day.
Part-time hours above contracted hours are treated as agreed flex-up hours. Hours that were not validly accepted as flex-up should be manually identified as overtime (clause 8.4).

Hours outside the ordinary span are treated as overtime. Where the employee has agreed to work those hours under a different arrangement, the user should apply the appropriate manual classification (clause 6.1(b)).

For an insufficient break, the calculator adds an amount equal to 100% of the base hourly rate to the affected hours. The result should be reviewed where another penalty or loading would otherwise apply, because the Agreement describes the entitlement as double the rate the employee would otherwise receive (clause 7.3).

Meal and rest breaks for shiftworkers are paid. Any break entered in the calculator is treated as unpaid and deducted from worked hours, so shiftworker breaks should be entered in line with the employee’s paid-break entitlement (clause 11.5).
Public holidays are selected by the user. The applicable date, location, substitution arrangements and shift-start treatment should be confirmed against the employee’s records and the Agreement.

exclusion_groups.title: Specific exclusions
items: The calculator reviews pay-period calculations only. Longer-period rules are outside the calculation, including the 144-hour part-time and 152-hour full-time limits, 19-day and 20-day roster arrangements, 16-day four-day-week arrangement, 9.5-hour four-day-week limit, consecutive-day rules, consecutive days off and regularly-worked-Sunday arrangements.
All employees are treated the same for shiftwork calculations. No special treatment is applied for baking-production employees, including their early-morning and night-shift rates.
Adult rates are used. Junior, apprentice, trainee, school-based apprentice and supported-wage rates are outside the calculation.

exclusion_groups.title: Other items not included
items: Classification progression, higher duties, future wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Meal-break compliance and payments, allowances, reimbursements, uniforms, meals, travel, vehicle use and other expenses, apart from the entered break deduction described above.
Recall payments, time off instead of overtime and minimum-payment rules not expressly configured.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Approval undertakings, saved provisions, annualised salaries, individual arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that alter the Agreement’s operation.

closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

coles_2024.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This model is a guide to selected adult employee payments under the Coles Retail Enterprise Agreement 2024. It applies the configured ordinary-hour spans, casual loading, minimum paid engagements for part-time and casual employees, weekday and weekend penalties, public-holiday rates, daily and period overtime thresholds, two-tier Monday-to-Saturday overtime rates, generic shiftwork rates and the configured break-between-work-periods rule.
assumptions: The selected instrument, classification, employment type, worker type, base hourly rate and entered shift details are correct, and the employee is a wages-paid team member covered by the Coles Retail Enterprise Agreement 2024.
The two entered weeks form one chronological fortnight. Full-time ordinary hours are assessed against 76 hours for that fortnight; part-time and casual period thresholds are assessed weekly.

The calculator applies the insufficient-break payment when the employee has less than 12 hours between work periods, on the assumption that the standard 12-hour gap applies and the employee has not selected the 10-hour Roster Choice.
Any part-time hours above the agreed pattern that are not manually marked as overtime are assumed to have been validly varied under the Agreement.

Selecting shiftworker means the employee is employed as a shiftworker, every submitted shift qualifies for the selected shiftwork treatment, and the employee is not rostered for a mixture of shiftwork and non-shiftwork in the same week.
Entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks, public-holiday selections and any manual ordinary-time or overtime selections accurately reflect the employee’s records and applicable arrangements.
A manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the entire entered shift, and the user has determined that classification is appropriate.
limitations: The calculator covers one 14-day period. It uses a 76-hour full-time threshold and a maximum of 10 worked days as fortnightly proxies, with the complete four-week roster tests and exact 5-day and 6-day/4-day pattern reserved for review against the roster.
The first entered shift exceeding 9 ordinary hours in a week is treated as the permitted shift of up to 11 ordinary hours. The user confirms that this is the rostered long day.

Part-time overtime outside the agreed or validly varied pattern is only partially represented. Weekly and daily thresholds are applied, but other hours outside the pattern must be manually marked as overtime.

Outside-span work is classified as overtime by default. Where clause 4.9.5 permits it to count as ordinary hours while retaining the applicable overtime rate, the result requires review because manual ordinary-time classification changes both its classification and payment treatment.
The break-between-work-periods calculation uses the standard 12-hour threshold. Employees who have selected the 10-hour Roster Choice require separate review.

Shiftworker meal and rest breaks are paid under the Agreement, but the calculator deducts any break entered as unpaid. The user must enter shiftworker breaks consistently with the applicable paid-break entitlement.
Public holidays are user-selected. The user confirms the applicable date, location, store-level substitution arrangements and shift-start treatment under the Agreement.
exclusions: The configured scope is limited to the rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above. Rules outside that scope include the examples below.
Voluntary Additional Shifts, including their consent, separate minimum engagements, break and recall treatment.
The 152-hour and 19-day or agreed 20-day four-week roster tests, maximum consecutive days, consecutive days off and regularly-worked-Sunday arrangements.
Baking-production shiftworker provisions and employee-specific saved provisions.
Junior and other special wage rates, classification progression, higher duties, future wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Meal-break compliance and payments, allowances, reimbursements, uniforms, meals, travel, vehicle use and other expenses, apart from the entered break deduction described above.
Recall payments, time off instead of overtime and minimum-payment rules not expressly configured.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Approval undertakings, saved provisions, annualised salaries, individual arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that alter the Agreement’s operation.
closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

gria_2026.title: Scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This model is a guide to selected adult employee payments under the General Retail Industry Award 2020. It applies the configured ordinary-hour spans, casual loading, casual minimum paid engagement, weekday and weekend penalties, public-holiday rates, daily and period overtime thresholds, two-tier Monday-to-Saturday overtime rates, generic shiftwork rates and the configured break-between-work-periods rule.
assumptions: The selected instrument, classification, employment type, worker type, base hourly rate and entered shift details are correct, and the employee is covered by the General Retail Industry Award 2020 without an enterprise agreement or other overriding arrangement.
The two entered weeks form one chronological fortnight. Full-time ordinary hours are assessed against 76 hours for that fortnight; part-time and casual period thresholds are assessed weekly.
The retailer’s trading hours satisfy clause 15.2(c), so the configured ordinary-hour span extends to 11:00 pm on every day.
Any part-time hours above guaranteed hours that are not manually marked as overtime are assumed to be covered by a valid variation to the employee’s guaranteed-hours arrangement.

Selecting shiftworker means the employee is specifically employed to perform shiftwork, every submitted shift qualifies for the selected shiftwork treatment, and the employee is not rostered for a mixture of shiftwork and non-shiftwork in the same week.

The calculator applies the insufficient-break payment when the employee has less than 12 hours between work periods, on the assumption that the standard 12-hour gap applies and no agreement reducing it to 10 hours is in place.
Entered start and finish times, unpaid breaks, public-holiday selections and any manual ordinary-time or overtime selections accurately reflect the employee’s records and applicable arrangements.
A manual ordinary-time or overtime selection applies to the entire entered shift, and the user has determined that classification is appropriate.
limitations: The calculator covers one 14-day period. It uses a 76-hour full-time threshold and a maximum of 10 worked days as fortnightly proxies, with other averaging arrangements and the Award’s exact weekly and four-week roster tests reserved for review against the roster.
The first entered shift exceeding 9 ordinary hours in a week is treated as the permitted shift of up to 11 ordinary hours. The user confirms that this is the rostered long day.
The configured 11:00 pm span assumes the retailer satisfies clause 15.2(c). Retailers with different trading hours require review against the applicable ordinary-hour span.

Part-time overtime outside guaranteed hours or a valid variation is only partially represented. Weekly and daily thresholds are applied, but other hours outside the arrangement must be manually marked as overtime.
Shiftworker mode applies the weekday shiftwork loading to all submitted Monday-to-Friday hours. The user confirms that the employee and each entered shift satisfy the Award’s shiftwork definitions.
The break-between-work-periods calculation uses the standard 12-hour threshold. An agreed reduction to 10 hours requires separate review.

Shiftworker meal and rest breaks are paid under the Award, but the calculator deducts any break entered as unpaid. The user must enter shiftworker breaks consistently with the applicable paid-break entitlement.
Public holidays are user-selected. The user confirms the applicable date, location and substitution arrangements.
exclusions: The configured scope is limited to the rules shown under ‘Show ruleset’ and described above. Rules outside that scope include the examples below.
The 1.5-hour minimum engagement for qualifying full-time secondary-school-student casuals.
Baking-production shiftworker provisions and the special newsagency and video-shop ordinary-hour spans.
Three-week, four-week and longer full-time averaging arrangements, the 19-day four-week limit and associated rostered-day-off arrangements.
Junior, apprentice, trainee, school-based apprentice and supported-wage rates.
Classification progression, higher duties, future annual wage changes and minimum-wage compliance.
Meal-break compliance and payments, allowances, reimbursements, uniforms, meals, travel, vehicle use and other expenses, apart from the entered break deduction described above.
Recall payments, time off instead of overtime and minimum-payment rules not expressly configured.
Leave, leave loading, superannuation, tax, deductions, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Enterprise agreements, annualised salaries, individual flexibility arrangements, employment-contract terms and other arrangements that may apply instead of, or alongside, the Award.
closing_paragraphs: These assumptions, limitations and exclusions must be checked against the employee’s actual employment arrangements, roster and payroll records.

qut_sessional.title: QUT Sessional scope and assumptions
paragraphs: This calculator estimates selected sessional academic activity payments under Schedules Two and Five of the QUT Academic Enterprise Agreement. It is limited to QUT sessional academic staff and does not calculate salaries or workload allocations for ongoing, fixed-term, teaching-intensive or QUT College appointments.
assumptions: The entered course, activity date, topic or teaching week, delivered quantity, direct hours and qualification or coordination status are correct.
Normal and repeat lecture or tutorial classification is based on matching course, activity and topic information supplied for the preceding seven calendar days.
Direct marking and other required academic activity hours were required or approved where the Agreement requires that approval.
The published rates effective from 13 December 2025 apply to the work entered. Earlier rate schedules are not included.
limitations: Browser-local history is used for the seven-day repeat lookback. Missing or cleared history may cause an activity to be classified as original unless the user records a reasoned override.
Actual associated hours are compared with incorporated time for review only. Exceeding incorporated time does not automatically create an additional payment.
The two-hour minimum engagement is reported as a potential shortfall by user-defined occasion. The calculator does not currently value that shortfall as an additional payment.
Dates and user-defined occasion groups are recorded, but clock times are not. Separate occasions on the same date must not be grouped unless they formed one occasion of required work.
exclusions: QUT College educators and non-sessional academic appointments.
Superannuation, tax, deductions, allowances, leave, termination payments, interest and back-pay calculations.
Industrial or factual determinations about whether work was required, approved, higher-level marking, the same subject matter, or covered by incorporated duties.
closing_paragraphs: Review the estimate against the applicable agreement, appointment documentation, activity allocation and university records before relying on it.
